newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - T-bond volatility edges up before FOMC.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - T-bond volatility edges up before FOMC.

text.p: Implied volatility for June U.S. Treasury bond options rose marginally Monday, one day before the Federal Open Market Committee is set to convene.
Options traders said bond volatility was limited by a lack of activity in the underlying futures, which finished the day 2/32 lower at 109-29 after trading in a narrow band between 110-03 and 109-23.
"There was no volume and nothing to trade on," said an options floor broker.
"Tomorrow will be more of the same," he added. The FOMC typically concludes its meeting in the early afternoon.
According to a Reuters poll, 21 of 39 primary dealers expect no change in U.S. short-term interest rates to result from the meeting.

Activity in bond options largely consisted of position squaring in preparation for Tuesday's main event, traders said. A few Wall Street dealer firms bought July calls in 110-00, 111-00 and 112-00 strikes, probably to offset previously placed positions, the traders said.
July volatility was quoted at 8.68 percent late in the session, up about 0.3 point from Friday, and September was 8.55 percent, down about 0.05 point, floor brokers said.
In Eurodollar options, volatility levels edged down from Friday, with December slipping 0.1 point to 11.4 percent.
A floor trader said the newly listed 94.125-strike June Eurodollar options were attracting a fair amount of interest as market participants positioned for Tuesday's Fed announcement.
